verdict.reasoning: Patient: "I've been having this, blinding headache for a few days... I find it very hard to focus or, like I can't even go to work." Headache duration clarified as three days: "that was three days ago, and I just keep having it."
Patient: "it just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago, and I just keep having it." and "Kinda all the time."
Doctor asks severity; patient: "I guess it's mostly, eight, and then it kinda comes down to maybe a five." and previously: "when I take Ibuprofen it gets a bit better... but then I still have it."
Patient: "it's kind of all over but, I feel like over my right eye, it's um bit, stronger." This supports holocephalic with right peri‑orbital predominance.

Photophobia: "lights definitely make me more sensitive... I don't really, like strong lights." Visual phenomena: "I get this, shooting light sometimes." Nausea without vomiting: "Uh, no, feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting."
Doctor: "Any tingling? Or numbness? Or weakness anywhere?" Patient: "Um, no." Doctor: "Any change in your smell or taste?" Patient: "No, none at all."

Positional/stabbing pain: "Sometimes when I stand up, quickly I get a bit of a, stabbing pain. Um, or if I throw my head like, it I kind of feel like something is moving inside." Sleep: "Um, yeah, I'm, sleeping well." and "Is it waking you up in the night-time?" Patient: "No, no, no. But I can wake up with it in the morning."

Fever: Doctor: "you haven't had a high temperature. Have you checked your temperature?" Patient: "Uh, no I didn't, I don't really feel, feverish or anything." URTI/sinus: "have you had any cold symptoms, sore throat, sore ears, or pain over the sinuses? Any cough or flem?" Patient: "No, no." Epistaxis/hemoptysis: "Any, any nose bleeds, or coughing up any blood or anything?" Patient: "No."

Prior headaches: "I recently had a, a one for like two days, um, but it just went away with Ibuprofen" and later "it's just um, a bit of a pressure, in between my eyes, um. But nothing major." Aura/N&V denied: Doctor: "Did you have any visual symptoms? Flashing lights? Nausea, vomiting with them?" Patient: "No... No, no... No nothing, none of those."
Doctor: "have you had any, uh, eye checks recently?" Patient: "yeah, actually had one recently and, nothing changed my vision." This implies no change in prescription.

Impact on work: initial: "I find it very hard to focus or, like I can't even go to work." Later: "I work from home but, couldn't really manage to, do it all the time. So sometimes I just took a day off... the second I just took the whole day off... today I just tried to work from home... but, I, I just stopped in the morning 'cause, I couldn't focus."

Doctor: "any other, medical problems in the past?" Patient: "I think I only had a, a pain, um, when I was younger but, no causes found and that went away, but that's, the only thing I know of." This supports no chronic conditions.
Patient: "Doesn't really go away with Ibuprofen either, I try that" and later: "apart from the Ibuprofen that I take, sometimes when, the headache gets really bad, nothing else."

Doctor: "Do you take any medications?" Patient: "just the pill." Doctor: "And when did you start that?" Patient: "about a year ago." Side effects: "Any side effects with that?" Patient: "Uh, no I don't think so." Brand unspecified in transcript, consistent with "unspecified."
Doctor: "any allergies to anything?" Patient: "No." This supports no known drug allergies.
Patient: "my mum, suffers from, like she has migraines... she has quite bad migraines, she's like, has the vomiting and everything."

Lives alone: "Who do you live with at home?" Patient: "just by myself." Smoking: "do you smoke?" Patient: "no." Alcohol: "Do you drink any alcohol regularly?" Patient: "Yeah... probably like, three , once a week." Drugs: "do you take any other drugs at all?" Patient: "no apart from the Ibuprofen... nothing else."
Doctor: "Have you been abroad recently at all?" Patient: "No."

Acute severe headache 3 days: "that was three days ago, and I just keep having it" and severity "mostly, eight"; photophobia and visual phenomena are documented. Doctor: "it could possibly be a migraine type headache." The phrasing "probable migraine with or without aura" is a clinical assessment consistent with discussion.
As above, patient is on an oral contraceptive pill: "just the pill" started a year ago; specific type not stated, matching "unspecified type."

Doctor: "we probably should, book you into an appointment to get an examination... we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well." This corresponds to in-person neuro exam and fundoscopy.
Doctor: "when you have a, an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well."

Doctor: "I can prescribe you something, similar to Ibuprofen, but a bit stronger which you can take instead of Ibuprofen... And start, the medication which I prescribe to you, take it with food." This is a stronger NSAID with food.
Doctor: "And you can also take Paracetamol at the same time."

Doctor: "if in the meantime before your appointment your, headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing. Then, if it's that bad, then you should go to A and E and have an examination... you can call us for further advice on that."
Doctor: "if it settles, in the meantime then, we can cancel that." referring to the appointment.
Doctor: "But you can carry on with that for the moment." referring to the current pill.

Doctor: "when you have a, an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well... because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights, and things like that." This indicates reassessing contraception and changing it if migraine with aura is confirmed.
